breakfast.name: Khachapuri Imeruli
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water, let stand 10 minutes.
Mix flour and salt, add yeast mixture and oil, knead into a soft dough.
Let dough rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the cheeses with one egg for the filling.
Divide dough into 4 pieces, flatten each into a circle.
Place cheese filling in the center, gather edges and seal.
Flatten gently into a disc and cook in a dry skillet over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes per side.
Brush with butter and serve hot.
breakfast.description: Georgia's iconic cheese-filled bread from the Imereti region, crispy outside with molten cheese inside.

breakfast.name: Chirbuli
ingredients: Salt and black pepper to taste
Crushed red pepper flakes to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Season with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Crack eggs into the tomato mixture, spacing them evenly.
Cover and cook until eggs are set to your liking.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and basil, serve with bread.
breakfast.description: Georgian-style eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce with fresh herbs, a comforting breakfast.

breakfast.name: Khachapuri Adjaruli (Adjarian Boat-Shaped Cheese Bread)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, yeast, water, salt, sugar, oil
Filling: 400g mixed cheese (sulguni + imeruli or mozzarella + feta)
1 egg per khachapuri (raw, cracked into the hot bread)
instructions: Make yeast dough, let rise 1 hour
Divide into portions, shape each into an oval
Roll out into a boat shape with raised edges — pinch the ends into points
Fill the boat with mixed cheese
Bake at 220°C for 12-15 min until dough is golden and cheese is melted and bubbling
Remove from oven, immediately crack a raw egg into the center of the molten cheese
Add a large knob of butter
Stir the egg and butter into the hot cheese at the table — it becomes a molten, creamy pool
Tear bread from the edges and dip into the cheese-egg-butter center
The cheese-pull when dipping bread is the most viral moment in Georgian food
This is NOT the same as regular khachapuri — the boat shape and the raw egg are Adjarian
breakfast.description: THE most viral Georgian food — a boat-shaped bread filled with molten cheese, a raw egg, and butter stirred together at the table into a golden, stretchy pool. The cheese-pull dipping videos have made Adjarian khachapuri one of the most searched food items on the internet. It represents everything that makes Georgian food legendary.

breakfast.name: Shotis Puri (Georgian Clay Oven Bread)
instructions: Make a soft, slightly wet dough
Let rise 1 hour
Shape into a long, canoe-like form with a twist
The baker reaches into the scorching-hot clay oven (tone) and slaps the bread onto the inner wall
The bread sticks to the wall and bakes in the radiant heat — 5-8 min
The baker reaches back in to pull the baked bread off the wall — this is a skill and a spectacle
The bread has a chewy, slightly charred exterior and a soft, airy interior
Fresh shotis puri from a tone is one of the great bread experiences in the world
Georgian bakeries have the ovens visible from the street — watching the baker is the show
breakfast.description: Georgian clay oven bread — the baker slaps dough onto the scorching inner wall of a clay tone oven, where it bakes in minutes. Watching the baker reach into the fiery oven is one of the most viral bakery videos from the Caucasus. The chewy, slightly charred bread is the foundation of every Georgian meal.

breakfast.name: Soko Ketsze (Mushrooms in Clay Pot)
instructions: Sauté mushrooms in butter with garlic until golden and all liquid evaporates
Season with salt, pepper, fresh herbs
Transfer to individual clay pots (ketsi)
Top with sliced sulguni cheese
Bake or broil until cheese is melted and bubbling — 5-8 min
The clay pot keeps everything sizzling at the table
Serve with shotis puri to scoop the cheesy mushrooms
The sizzling clay pot presentation is dramatic and the cheese-mushroom stretch is satisfying
breakfast.description: Mushrooms sautéed in butter and topped with melted sulguni cheese, served sizzling in a clay pot — a Georgian breakfast or appetizer that showcases the country's love of cheese and clay-pot cooking. The sizzle and the cheese pull are viral, and the earthenware presentation is quintessentially Georgian.

lunch.name: Kharcho
ingredients: 4 tablespoons tkemali (sour plum sauce) or tomato paste
instructions: Brown beef cubes in a large pot, then add broth and bring to a boil.
Skim any foam, reduce heat, and simmer for 1 hour.
Sauté onions until golden, add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add onion mixture, rice, tkemali, and ground walnuts to the pot.
Stir in khmeli-suneli, coriander, and bay leaf.
Simmer for 20 minutes until rice is cooked.
Stir in fresh cilantro, adjust seasoning, and serve hot.
lunch.description: A rich and tangy Georgian beef soup with walnuts, rice, and sour plum sauce.

lunch.name: Lobio
ingredients: 2 cups dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Boil soaked beans in fresh water until very tender, about 30 minutes.
Drain beans, reserving 1 cup of cooking liquid.
Mash about half the beans with a fork.
Sauté onion until soft, add garlic and spices.
Combine beans, onion mixture, ground walnuts, and reserved liquid.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in vinegar and cilantro, serve with cornbread.
lunch.description: A hearty spiced kidney bean stew with walnuts and fresh herbs, a staple of Georgian cuisine.

lunch.name: Pkhali (Vegetable-Walnut Pâté)
ingredients: Vegetables: spinach, beet tops, or green beans (each prepared separately)
Walnut paste: 200g walnuts, garlic, cilantro, fenugreek, red pepper, vinegar
instructions: Blanch or cook chosen vegetable until tender, squeeze out all water
Grind walnuts with garlic, cilantro, fenugreek, red pepper, vinegar into a thick paste
Mix the walnut paste into the chopped vegetable — every piece should be coated
Shape into small round patties or balls
Garnish each with pomegranate seeds — the red on green is the visual signature
Serve as part of a Georgian supra (feast) spread — multiple colors of pkhali together
Traditional to make three varieties: green (spinach), red (beet), white (green bean)
The tri-color pkhali platter is one of Georgia's most photogenic dishes
lunch.description: Georgia's walnut-vegetable pâté — blanched vegetables bound with a garlicky walnut paste, shaped into patties and studded with pomegranate seeds. The tri-color platter (green spinach, red beet, white bean) is one of the most photographed Georgian feast dishes. Viral in plant-based food circles as an ancient vegan tradition.

lunch.name: Ostri (Spicy Beef Stew)
instructions: Brown beef cubes in batches — deep golden crust
Sauté onion until soft, add garlic
Add tomato paste, cook until dark
Add blended tomatoes, adjika, fenugreek, khmeli suneli, bay leaf
Return beef, add water to just cover
Simmer 1-1.5 hours until beef is fork-tender
The sauce should be thick, dark red, and intensely spiced
Add massive amounts of fresh herbs — cilantro, parsley, basil — in the last 5 min
The herbs must be fresh and abundant — this is Georgia's herb philosophy
Serve with bread for soaking up the sauce
lunch.description: Georgia's fiery beef stew — tender cubes braised in a spicy tomato-adjika sauce with an avalanche of fresh herbs added at the end. Georgia's philosophy of drowning food in fresh herbs (cilantro, parsley, basil by the handful) has gone viral as a flavor philosophy the rest of the world is just catching up to.

lunch.name: Ajapsandali (Georgian Ratatouille)
instructions: Fry cubed eggplant until golden — in batches so it browns, doesn't steam
Sauté onion and peppers
Add tomatoes, garlic — cook until saucy
Return eggplant, combine everything
Simmer 15-20 min until vegetables meld together
Add enormous amounts of fresh herbs — this is not a garnish, it's a major ingredient
Season with salt and hot pepper
Serve warm or at room temperature
The herb-to-vegetable ratio should be shocking to non-Georgians — they use that much
lunch.description: Georgia's herb-loaded vegetable stew — like ratatouille but buried under an almost unreasonable amount of fresh basil, cilantro, and parsley. The 'how much fresh herbs can you put in one dish' challenge is what makes Georgian cooking viral — more than you think, and then more.

dinner.name: Khinkali
ingredients: 1/2 cup cold water or broth for filling
instructions: Make dough with flour, water, and salt; knead until smooth, rest 30 minutes.
Mix meat with onion, garlic, cilantro, cumin, pepper, salt, and cold water.
Roll dough thin and cut into 4-inch circles.
Place a heaping tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle.
Pleat the edges together forming a gathered top knot, twist to seal.
Boil in large pot of salted water for 10 to 12 minutes.
Eat by holding the knot, biting a hole, sipping the broth inside, then eating the rest. Discard the knot.
dinner.description: Iconic Georgian soup dumplings with a spiced meat filling that creates its own broth inside.

dinner.name: Chicken Tabaka
instructions: Rub the spatchcocked chicken with garlic, coriander, paprika, pepper, and salt.
Heat butter and oil in a large heavy skillet over medium heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Press down with a heavy lid or another skillet weighted with a can.
Cook for 15 to 18 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip and cook for another 15 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with tkemali sauce and fresh herbs.
dinner.description: Pressed and pan-fried whole chicken with an impossibly crispy skin, a Georgian classic.

dinner.name: Mtsvadi (Georgian Grilled Meat Skewers)
ingredients: 1.5kg pork, beef, or lamb (large cubes — bigger than typical kebab)
Pomegranate juice or dry red wine (for marinade)
instructions: Cut meat into large cubes — 4-5cm, bigger than most kebab traditions
Marinate in onion, pomegranate juice or wine, salt, pepper — at least 2 hours
Thread onto flat metal skewers — Georgian skewers are sword-like
Grill over charcoal — traditionally using dried grapevine cuttings as fuel, which adds a subtle wine-smoke flavor
Turn only when the bottom is deeply charred — do not fuss with them
The outside should be charred, the inside juicy and pink
Serve on a bed of raw onion rings with tkemali (sour plum sauce)
At a Georgian feast (supra), mtsvadi is the main event — the grill master (metskhvare) has an honored role
The grilling is always done outdoors, by men, and is deeply social
dinner.description: Georgian grilled meat — large cubes charred over grapevine cuttings, served with sour plum sauce. The grapevine-smoke technique, the sword-like skewers, and the social ritual of outdoor grilling at a Georgian supra have made mtsvadi viral. Georgian BBQ has its own philosophy: big cubes, high heat, sour sauce.

dinner.name: Shkmeruli (Garlic Cream Chicken)
ingredients: Massive amount of garlic — 2 full heads (20+ cloves), roughly crushed
instructions: Spatchcock the chicken — remove backbone, press flat
Season generously with salt and pepper
Sear in butter in a hot pan, skin-side down, until deeply golden
Flip, sear other side
Transfer to a baking dish or clay pot
Crush 20+ cloves of garlic — roughly, not minced
Scatter garlic around and over the chicken
Pour milk or cream around the chicken
Bake at 190°C for 30-35 min until chicken is cooked through and garlic is soft
The garlic melts into the cream, creating a sauce that is INTENSELY garlicky
Serve straight from the clay pot with bread to soak up the garlic cream
The amount of garlic is not a typo — Georgians mean it
dinner.description: Whole chicken drowned in an obscene amount of garlic and cream — Georgia's most viral chicken dish. The 20+ cloves of garlic melt into the cream to create a sauce so garlicky it clears sinuses. The 'that much garlic?!' shock factor and the clay-pot presentation have made shkmeruli a global sensation.

dinner.name: Chakapuli (Spring Lamb Stew)
ingredients: Tkemali (sour green plums — unripe) or sour plum sauce
Fresh tarragon (a LOT — this is the star herb)
instructions: Brown lamb pieces
Add dry white wine — generous pour
Add sour green plums or tkemali
Add all the green herbs — tarragon especially, by the fistful
Add green onions and green chili
The stew should be bright green from all the herbs — this is a green stew
Simmer 40-45 min until lamb is tender and the sauce is sour-herby
The tarragon flavor should dominate — this is Georgia's spring celebration dish
Serve with bread
Made in spring when wild tarragon and sour plums are in season — deeply seasonal
dinner.description: Georgia's spring celebration stew — lamb simmered in white wine with sour plums and an enormous amount of fresh tarragon. The stew is bright GREEN from the herbs. Chakapuli represents Georgia's seasonal, herb-forward philosophy at its peak. The shocking green color and the 'how much tarragon?!' reaction are viral.

dinner.name: Satsivi (Walnut Sauce Chicken — Cold)
ingredients: Walnut sauce: 500g walnuts, garlic (6+ cloves), onion, cinnamon, cloves, fenugreek, coriander, saffron
instructions: Poach or roast chicken until cooked, cut into pieces
Grind walnuts with garlic, spices (cinnamon, cloves, fenugreek, coriander, saffron) into a fine paste
Sauté onion, add walnut paste and chicken broth — stir into a thick, creamy sauce
Add vinegar for tang
Temper egg yolks into the sauce for richness and silk
Pour the thick walnut sauce over the chicken pieces
Let cool completely — satsivi is served COLD
The sauce thickens as it cools, coating every piece in a thick, spiced walnut cream
Refrigerate overnight — the flavors develop and deepen
This is Georgia's Christmas and New Year's dish — the holiday table must have satsivi
dinner.description: Georgia's cold walnut-sauce chicken — poached chicken buried under a thick, spiced walnut cream sauce and served cold. Traditionally the New Year's centerpiece. The concept of deliberately cold chicken in thick nut sauce surprises people outside the Caucasus and the rich, complex walnut sauce has made satsivi viral as a unique holiday dish.

snacks.name: Badrijani Nigvzit
instructions: Salt eggplant slices and let sit 20 minutes, pat dry.
Fry eggplant in oil until golden on both sides, drain on paper towels.
Grind walnuts, garlic, cilantro, coriander, and fenugreek into a paste.
Add vinegar and salt, mix well.
Spread walnut paste on each eggplant slice.
Roll up each slice tightly.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds and serve at room temperature.
snacks.description: Fried eggplant rolls filled with a garlicky walnut-herb paste, a quintessential Georgian appetizer.

snacks.name: Lobiani (Bean-Filled Bread)
ingredients: Filling: cooked kidney beans (mashed), onion, suneli spices
instructions: Make yeast dough, let rise 1 hour
Cook and mash kidney beans — keep some texture
Sauté onion, mix into beans with suneli spices
Roll out dough into rounds, fill generously with bean mixture
Seal and flatten into a round bread — the filling should be distributed evenly
Bake at 200°C for 15-20 min until golden
Brush with butter immediately when out of the oven
Cut into wedges — the bean filling should be thick and spiced throughout
This is the bean version of khachapuri — equally beloved, less internationally famous
snacks.description: Georgia's bean-filled flatbread — the lesser-known sibling of khachapuri, stuffed with spiced mashed kidney beans instead of cheese. Equally beloved in Georgia, lobiani deserves the same viral fame. The bean filling spiced with suneli is hearty and satisfying.

snacks.name: Elarji (Cheesy Cornmeal — Georgia's 'Fondue')
instructions: Boil water with salt
Add cornmeal gradually, stirring constantly
Cook on low heat, stirring with a wooden spoon for 15-20 min until very thick
Add shredded sulguni cheese — a LOT of it
Stir vigorously — the cheese melts and creates long, dramatic cheese pulls
Keep stirring until the cheese and cornmeal are completely integrated — it's stretchy and gooey
Serve immediately — scoop with bread or eat with a spoon
The cheese-pull when lifting a spoon is the most dramatic in all of Georgian food
This is Mingrelian (western Georgia) comfort food — pure cheese-and-carb bliss
snacks.description: Georgia's cheese-cornmeal mash — so much sulguni cheese is stirred in that the result is stretchy, gooey, and pulls like fondue. The cheese-pull videos when lifting a spoon from elarji are the most dramatic in Georgian food content. Mingrelian comfort food in its purest, most excessive form.

snacks.name: Mchadi (Cornbread)
instructions: Mix cornmeal with water or milk and salt — dough should be firm enough to shape
Shape into flat, thick patties
Fry in butter or oil on medium heat until golden and crusty on both sides — 5-6 min per side
Or bake on a clay pan for a drier, crunchier version
The outside should be crunchy, the inside dense and corny
Serve hot with slices of sulguni cheese — the classic pairing
Mchadi and cheese is Georgia's equivalent of bread and butter — the simplest, most comforting combination
snacks.description: Georgian fried cornbread — dense, crunchy-crusted cornmeal patties served with slices of sulguni cheese. The simplest Georgian food and the one that says 'home.' The cornbread-and-cheese combination is Georgia's answer to bread and butter.

snacks.name: Gebzhalia (Cheese Rolls in Mint Sauce)
ingredients: Sauce: matsoni (Georgian yogurt) or sour cream, garlic, fresh mint, chili flakes
instructions: Heat sulguni until soft and pliable
Shape into thin rolls or fold into rectangles while warm
Let cheese cool and firm up
Make sauce: mix matsoni/sour cream with crushed garlic, chopped fresh mint, chili flakes, vinegar, salt
Pour sauce over cheese rolls — the white cheese in green-speckled sauce is beautiful
Refrigerate — serve cold
The cool, minty, garlicky sauce against the mild cheese is refreshing and addictive
A Mingrelian specialty that showcases Georgia's creative use of fresh cheese
snacks.description: Fresh sulguni cheese rolled and bathed in a cold mint-garlic-yogurt sauce — a Mingrelian appetizer that's refreshing, tangy, and beautiful (white cheese in green-speckled sauce). The creative use of cheese beyond melting has made gebzhalia viral as an example of Georgia's cheese artistry.

desserts.name: Churchkhela
instructions: Thread nuts onto 12-inch lengths of strong thread using a needle.
Heat grape juice in a pot until warm.
Mix flour and cornstarch, whisk into the grape juice gradually.
Add sugar and cook on medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens like pudding.
Dip each nut string into the thickened juice, coating evenly.
Hang the coated strings to dry for a few hours, then dip again.
Repeat dipping 3 to 4 times, then hang to dry for 5 to 7 days until firm but chewy.
desserts.description: Traditional Georgian candle-shaped candy made of nuts dipped in thickened grape juice, a holiday treat.

desserts.name: Pelamushi (Grape Juice Pudding)
ingredients: 2L fresh grape juice (Saperavi or other dark grape — must be fresh, not store-bought)
Sugar (if needed — ripe grape juice may be sweet enough)
instructions: Mix cornstarch with a cup of cold grape juice until smooth
Bring remaining grape juice to a boil
Slowly pour the starch mixture into the boiling juice, stirring constantly
Cook on medium heat, stirring, until thick and glossy — like a thick pudding
Pour into molds or plates
Embed walnut halves on top while still warm
Let cool and set — it firms to a jelly-like consistency
Serve cold — the deep purple color is stunning
Pelamushi is also the base for churchkhela — the walnut strings are dipped in this same mixture
Made during rtveli (grape harvest) season when fresh grape juice is abundant
desserts.description: Georgian grape juice pudding — fresh grape juice thickened into a deep purple, jelly-like dessert. Also the base for churchkhela (the famous walnut-grape 'candles'). Made during rtveli (grape harvest), Georgia's most important seasonal food tradition. The stunning purple color and the harvest ritual are viral.

desserts.name: Gozinaki (Honey-Walnut Brittle)
instructions: Toast walnuts lightly — they should be fragrant but not dark
Heat honey and sugar until it reaches hard-crack stage — this takes patience and a thermometer helps
Add toasted walnuts, stir quickly to coat
Pour onto a surface dusted with powdered sugar
Flatten to about 1cm thick while hot
Score into diamond shapes before it fully hardens
Let cool completely — it becomes a crunchy, honey-glazed nut brittle
These are Georgia's New Year's sweets — every family makes gozinaki for the holiday table
The combination of Georgian mountain honey and fresh walnuts is simple but extraordinary
desserts.description: Georgia's New Year's candy — fresh walnuts locked in crystallized honey, cut into diamond shapes. Every Georgian family makes gozinaki for the holiday table. The crunch, the floral honey flavor, and the diamond-cutting tradition are viral elements of Georgian holiday food culture.

desserts.name: Tklapi (Fruit Leather)
ingredients: Sour plums (tkemali plums), or sour cherries, or apricots
Sugar (minimal or none — the fruit flavor should dominate)
instructions: Cook fruit until completely soft and broken down
Push through a sieve to remove skins and pits — you want a smooth purée
Add minimal sugar if needed — the fruit should taste like concentrated fruit
Spread the purée very thin on a cloth or silicone sheet — as thin as possible
Dry in the sun for several hours (traditional) or in a low oven (65°C) for 6-8 hours
The leather should be pliable but not sticky
Roll up and store — it keeps for months
Tklapi is used as a souring agent in Georgian cooking — dissolved into stews and sauces
It's both a snack (eaten as fruit leather) and a pantry staple (dissolved for acidity)
desserts.description: Georgia's dual-purpose fruit leather — eaten as a snack AND dissolved into stews as a souring agent. Sun-dried from sour plum purée, it represents Georgia's genius for preserving the harvest. The sun-drying technique and the 'it's a snack and a cooking ingredient' concept are viral in the food-preservation community.

drinks.name: Tarkhuna Lemonade
instructions: Muddle tarragon leaves in a bowl to release oils.
Make a simple syrup by boiling 1 cup water with sugar until dissolved.
Add muddled tarragon to the hot syrup, steep for 15 minutes.
Strain the tarragon syrup into a pitcher.
Add lemon juice and chill.
Top with cold sparkling water and serve over ice.
drinks.description: A bright green tarragon-flavored sparkling lemonade, Georgia's beloved herbal soft drink.

drinks.name: Saperavi Wine
ingredients: Traditional clay cups or wine glasses
instructions: Select a quality Saperavi wine, ideally from the Kakheti region.
Open the bottle and let it breathe for 15 to 20 minutes.
Pour into traditional clay cups or wine glasses.
Serve at cellar temperature, about 16 to 18 degrees Celsius.
Enjoy alongside Georgian cheese and bread as part of a supra feast.
drinks.description: Georgia's signature deep ruby-red wine made from the ancient Saperavi grape, enjoyed at traditional feasts.

drinks.name: Chacha (Georgian Grape Brandy)
ingredients: Grape pomace (skins, seeds, stems left over from winemaking)
instructions: Combine grape pomace with water, let ferment for 2-3 weeks in a warm place
The pomace ferments into a low-alcohol wine
Distill the fermented pomace — this requires a copper still
Collect the 'heart' of the distillation — discard the heads and tails
The result is a clear, potent spirit — typically 40-65% alcohol
Age in clay qvevri or drink fresh (young chacha is most common)
Every rural Georgian family makes their own chacha — it's a cottage industry
Chacha is served at every supra (feast) — the tamada (toastmaster) pours generously
Used medicinally, socially, and in cooking — it is the spirit of Georgia, literally
drinks.description: Georgia's fiery grape brandy — distilled from the pomace left over from qvevri winemaking. Every rural family makes their own. At a Georgian supra feast, the tamada pours chacha for elaborate toasts. The homemade-distillery culture and the supra toast traditions are viral elements of Georgian drinking culture.

drinks.name: Kompot (Fruit Compote Drink)
ingredients: Mixed fruits: peaches, plums, cherries, apples, pears — whatever is in season
instructions: Wash and halve or quarter fruits — leave some pits in for flavor
Bring water and sugar to a simmer
Add fruit, simmer 15-20 min until fruit is soft and liquid is fruity and sweet
Let cool — serve cold with some of the cooked fruit in each glass
The color depends on the fruit — cherry kompot is deep red, peach is golden
Every Georgian grandmother makes kompot in summer — it's the house drink
Stored in jars on shelves — the pantry lined with jewel-colored kompot jars is a Georgian aesthetic
drinks.description: Georgian fruit compote drink — fresh seasonal fruits simmered in sweet water, served cold. Every grandmother's shelf lined with jewel-colored jars of kompot is a viral Georgian home aesthetic. The simplicity (fruit + water + sugar) and the seasonal variety make kompot a symbol of Georgian hospitality.
